audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed between layers and against the packet chart: phases[4].side said 'Skill' while win[4] said 'Aatrox', and phases[6].side said 'Nautilus' while win[6] said 'Skill'. Levels 1-2 were given to Aatrox in both layers even though both whys[0] and whys[1] describe a coin-flip.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Skill/Aatrox/Aatrox/Aatrox/Aatrox/Skill and win rate is 47.83% over 23 games — close to even, tilting Aatrox mid. The prose already said levels 1-2 were even.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Skill, Aatrox, Aatrox, Aatrox, Aatrox, Skill in BOTH layers, proposed as matched pairs, with ratings realigned (5/10 on Skill rows, 4/10 on Aatrox rows).

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes and whys leaned on 'Eclipse/Goredrinker' as Aatrox's first item, an item pair I cannot verify as current on patch 26.15, and no Grievous Wounds timing was tied to the spike.
audit.why: The missingInteractions entry flags anti-heal as the decider for extended trades (Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash, World Ender all heal). Naming a possibly-dead item is a fabrication risk; the spike itself is real.
audit.corrected: Item names replaced with 'first item' / 'first-item spike', and the spike now states that Grievous Wounds must land before it to keep the grind honest. Nautilus spikes kept: level 2-3 pattern, level 6 Depth Charge, first item, 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text claimed Depth Charge 'cancels his R animation'. World Ender is not a channel and has no cancellable cast in Riot's description. Aatrox's W was described only as 'W chain-pull' with no name and no cooldown, and Nautilus's passive was never named.
audit.why: Kit text authority: World Ender is an instant transformation buff, so there is no animation to interrupt — Depth Charge locks him down but does not undo the ult. Infernal Chains (W) drags and slows; the derived 'grounding' flag on it is not supported by Riot's text, so no grounding claim is made (the mirror audit reached the same conclusion). Deathbringer Stance (P) is an auto-attack reset that heals off max health — the wind-up, not a cast, is the tell.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge restated as undodgeable lockdown that lands through Umbral Dash (E) and holds him after World Ender rather than cancelling it. Infernal Chains named with its 20s rank-1 cooldown as the bait target. Deathbringer Stance named as the auto-reset tell and as the reason anti-heal is core. Staggering Blow named for the level-1 first-attack root. The Darkin Blade cooldowns (14s at rank 1 down to 6s at rank 5) and Nautilus Q's 14s rank-1 cooldown added where advice needed to be concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed 'your committal tool' generically and gave no numbers.
audit.why: The two punishable windows are The Darkin Blade between chains and Infernal Chains at 20s rank 1 — real numbers make the advice actionable.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].d ('Eat his Q3 knockup') gave no tell for when the combo is starting.
audit.why: The combo opens on a Deathbringer Stance auto reset, not on an ability cast — that is the actual mistake players make.
audit.corrected: Don't now names the auto-reset wind-up as the step-back cue.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin-flip — neither of us has a real all-in, but my passive root on the first auto means I win the auto-for-auto exchange if he steps up to last-hit. Don't throw Q blind; he'll just dodge it and I'm left with no engage and no escape for its long cooldown. Once I hit Level 3 with Q, W and E I can finally answer him: Q-pull him in, passive-root, W shield-burn one rotation, E-slow, and walk out before his heal-on-hit turns it around. The whole early game is about keeping trades short — if I let his three Q knockups and passive sustain stack, the math flips even when I started ahead.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin-flip — neither of us has a real all-in, but Staggering Blow rooting on my first attack means I win the auto-for-auto exchange if he steps up to last-hit. Don't throw Q blind; he'll just dodge it and I'm left with no engage and no escape for a full 14 seconds. Once I hit Level 3 with Q, W and E I can finally answer him: Q-pull him in, passive-root, W shield-burn one rotation, E-slow, and walk out before Deathbringer Stance turns it around. The whole early game is about keeping trades short — if I let his three Darkin Blade knockups and that max-health heal stack, the math flips even when I started ahead.

edits.before: This is where he takes over. His Eclipse/Goredrinker timing means a long trade now heals him back to full, so I cannot sit in his Q sweetspots and brawl — my W burn and base damage just don't out-DPS a healing Aatrox once items land. My Level 6 is my one real swing: Depth Charge is an undodgeable knock-up that ignores his dashes, so I hold it to interrupt his R all-in or to pin him for my jungler rather than blowing it for chip. Bait his W chain-pull — once it's down he can't reposition me, and that's my window to Q-pull-and-leave instead of getting dragged onto his sweetspots.
edits.after: This is where he takes over. His first-item timing means a long trade heals him back to full, so I cannot sit in The Darkin Blade's sweetspots and brawl — a Bramble Vest bought before that item is what keeps my grind honest. My Level 6 is my one real swing: Depth Charge is an undodgeable knock-up that lands through Umbral Dash, so I hold it to pin him for my jungler rather than blowing it for chip. Bait Infernal Chains — it is down 20 seconds at rank 1, and without it he cannot drag me back onto the sweetspots I just walked out of.

edits.after: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: 14s at rank 1 down to 6s at rank 5 — the third swing knocks up, so sidestep it. - Infernal Chains: 20s at rank 1 — bait it, then step in. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's own description does not support (drag to centre plus slow only) — no grounding claim was made, matching the mirror audit on aatrox__nautilus. 'Eclipse/Goredrinker' appeared in three fields as Aatrox's first item; I could not verify either item is current on patch 26.15, so I replaced the names with 'first item' rather than substituting a guess. Umbral Dash charge behaviour and whether Depth Charge can be QSS'd or cleansed are not in the kit files and were not asserted.
